{"cohort_definition": "Final Cohort Definition

1) Index event:
   - Domain: Measurement.
   - Concept set intent: Influenza virus laboratory tests (e.g., influenza A/B PCR, influenza antigen tests) capturing laboratory measurements/tests indicating influenza infection.
   - Use standard concepts only.
   - Include descendants: Yes (include descendant measurement concepts of the selected influenza test concepts).

2) Entry criteria:
   - Qualification event: The first qualifying influenza laboratory measurement per person occurring within the index period (see item 5).
   - First-ever vs first-in-window: First-in-window (first qualifying measurement during the 2020 calendar-year window).
   - Washout days: No washout required for entry (0 days).
   - Minimum prior observation: 0 days (no minimum prior observation required).

3) Population constraints:
   - Age at index: Include persons whose age at index date is >= 20 and <= 40 (inclusive).
   - Sex: Restrict to male persons only (as recorded in the standard PERSON.sex_concept_id values representing male).
   - Additional inclusion filters: None.

4) Visit/setting restrictions:
   - None. Do not restrict to inpatient/outpatient/ED settings. Any care setting for the measurement is allowed.

5) Time window for index:
   - Allowed index dates: Any date from 2020-01-01 through 2020-12-31 (inclusive). Only measurements within this calendar-year window qualify.

6) Exclusions:
   - No additional exclusion criteria specified. (Pregnancy exclusions not applicable because cohort is restricted to males.)

7) Cohort exit and deduplication rules:
   - Cohort exit: Cohort end = index date (i.e., end of the same day as the qualifying measurement). This treats each qualifying person as a single cohort member at their first-in-window measurement.
   - Deduplication/episode rules: Limit one cohort entry per person (use first qualifying measurement in the 2020 window). Counting objective: count unique persons (one per person at most).

8) Notes / Assumptions:
   - Assumption: "Lab-confirmed influenza" will be operationalized as a laboratory test measurement for influenza where the recorded result indicates infection (e.g., result/value concept indicating 'positive', 'detected', or equivalent).    - Assumption: The influenza measurement concept set will include common influenza laboratory test concepts (PCR, molecular, antigen) as standard measurement concepts and will include descendants.    - Assumption: No minimum prior observation period is required to maximize capture; if the implementer prefers to require baseline history for covariate capture, set a prior observation requirement (commonly 365 days) — but none is required here per user request.
   - Assumption: Use standard OMOP sex_concept_id for male only; include persons whose sex at index is male.

Implementation guidance for ATLAS (concise, not pseudocode):
   - Build a Measurement concept set for influenza laboratory tests (standard concepts only, include descendants).
   - Add a measurement criteria in ATLAS: measurement of any concept in that influenza measurement concept set, with value_as_concept indicating positive/detected (include mapped synonyms/descendants for "positive/detected").
   - Restrict the measurement occurrence date to 2020-01-01 through 2020-12-31.
   - Add age restriction at index: 20 to 40 inclusive; add sex filter: male only.
   - Set cohort entry to first measurement in window per person and restrict to one entry per person.
   - Set cohort exit to index date.

End of definition.", "refinement_feedback": ""}

scratchpad.cohort_definition:
Final Cohort Definition

1) Index event:
   - Domain: Measurement.
   - Concept set intent: Influenza virus laboratory tests (e.g., influenza A/B PCR, influenza antigen tests) capturing laboratory measurements/tests indicating influenza infection.
   - Use standard concepts only.
   - Include descendants: Yes (include descendant measurement concepts of the selected influenza test concepts).

2) Entry criteria:
   - Qualification event: The first qualifying influenza laboratory measurement per person occurring within the index period (see item 5).
   - First-ever vs first-in-window: First-in-window (first qualifying measurement during the 2020 calendar-year window).
   - Washout days: No washout required for entry (0 days).
   - Minimum prior observation: 0 days (no minimum prior observation required).

3) Population constraints:
   - Age at index: Include persons whose age at index date is >= 20 and <= 40 (inclusive).
   - Sex: Restrict to male persons only (as recorded in the standard PERSON.sex_concept_id values representing male).
   - Additional inclusion filters: None.

4) Visit/setting restrictions:
   - None. Do not restrict to inpatient/outpatient/ED settings. Any care setting for the measurement is allowed.

5) Time window for index:
   - Allowed index dates: Any date from 2020-01-01 through 2020-12-31 (inclusive). Only measurements within this calendar-year window qualify.

6) Exclusions:
   - No additional exclusion criteria specified. (Pregnancy exclusions not applicable because cohort is restricted to males.)

7) Cohort exit and deduplication rules:
   - Cohort exit: Cohort end = index date (i.e., end of the same day as the qualifying measurement). This treats each qualifying person as a single cohort member at their first-in-window measurement.
   - Deduplication/episode rules: Limit one cohort entry per person (use first qualifying measurement in the 2020 window). Counting objective: count unique persons (one per person at most).

8) Notes / Assumptions:
   - Assumption: "Lab-confirmed influenza" will be operationalized as a laboratory test measurement for influenza where the recorded result indicates infection (e.g., result/value concept indicating 'positive', 'detected', or equivalent). Only measurements with an explicit positive/detected result are included. Tests with missing or non-positive results will be excluded.
   - Assumption: The influenza measurement concept set will include common influenza laboratory test concepts (PCR, molecular, antigen) as standard measurement concepts and will include descendants. Implementer should construct a concept set for influenza lab tests using standard OMOP measurement concepts and include descendants.
   - Assumption: For result/value mapping, the ATLAS definition should require value_as_concept_id corresponding to standard concepts representing "Positive"/"Detected" (and descendants), or value_as_number/text thresholds only if a validated mapping exists in the source. If multiple result representations exist in the source, include all standard-concept mappings that represent a positive/detected result.
   - Assumption: No minimum prior observation period is required to maximize capture; if the implementer prefers to require baseline history for covariate capture, set a prior observation requirement (commonly 365 days) — but none is required here per user request.
   - Assumption: Use standard OMOP sex_concept_id for male only; include persons whose sex at index is male.

Implementation guidance for ATLAS (concise, not pseudocode):
   - Build a Measurement concept set for influenza laboratory tests (standard concepts only, include descendants).
   - Add a measurement criteria in ATLAS: measurement of any concept in that influenza measurement concept set, with value_as_concept indicating positive/detected (include mapped synonyms/descendants for "positive/detected").
   - Restrict the measurement occurrence date to 2020-01-01 through 2020-12-31.
   - Add age restriction at index: 20 to 40 inclusive; add sex filter: male only.
   - Set cohort entry to first measurement in window per person and restrict to one entry per person.
   - Set cohort exit to index date.

End of definition.
